item.title: Socialist Wisconsin governor candidate referred to America as 'abundance of suffering,' resurfaced post shows
item.description: Fox News Digital found Francesca Hong's X posts calling America "an abundance of suffering" and urging police abolition in her governor campaign.
item.content:encoded:
A socialist candidate for governor in Wisconsin with an extensive history of inflammatory online posts once described America as "an abundance of suffering," Fox News Digital has found.

"I want this country to stop being an abundance of suffering but a wealth of opportunity," reads a Jan. 20, 2022 X post from Wisconsin state Rep. Francesca Hong, who is running in the Democratic Party's primary election to become the state's top official.

"We can do this by providing equal rights to Black and Brown folks," the post continues. "Elect more Black and Brown folks who won't be racist obstructionists. We can all be better and do so much more."

SOCIALIST FRONTRUNNER IN THE HOT SEAT AFTER 'CANCEL THANKSGIVING' POST EMERGES ONLINE

This isn't the first time the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) candidate has faced scrutiny for past comments on social media that are especially critical of America and its institutions and ideals.

"Cancel Thanksgiving. Should have done this in 1621," Hong wrote in a now-deleted post on X.

"If it takes a worldwide pandemic for us to realize we should stop celebrating colonialism and the original superspreader event that killed indigenous folx [sic] and women, so be it," she added, referring to the spread of smallpox that killed many indigenous Americans.

Despite a string of posts, the former chef and mother-of-one, is now running for the Democratic nomination for governor in Wisconsin. She's the latest in a strong of socialists seeking statewide or federal office in this year's primary against establishment Democrats.

LEFT’S LATEST SOCIALIST DARLING DRAGGED OVER ‘WHITENESS’ COMMENTS PULLING IN HER OWN FAMILY: ‘WEIRDO RACISM’

Hong, who is Korean America, also said in a 2019 post that she was anxious in the company of White people.

"I ate two bites of my kid's cheeseburger at a Culver's in black river falls and told him they ran out of ice cream," that post said. "Mostly just wanted to leave bc I was on the verge of a anxiety attack...to (sic) many old white people who didn't think we spoke english."

When prosecutors declined to press charges in 2021 for the high-profile shooting of Jacob Blake in August 2020, in Kenosha, Wisc., Hong joined the chorus of left-wing voicing calling to abolish police.

"How is 7 bullets in the back not excessive force," she said at the time. "Police exist to uphold White supremacy. Defund then abolish. Reform can't be an option. My heart breaks for the trauma the Blake family and their community continues to endure."

TOP WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST CANDIDATE CONFRONTED ON PAST 'DEFUND POLICE' RHETORIC

Hong's team declined in July to walk back her position on police.

"Rep. Hong has spoken in the past about police and prison abolition as an aspirational goal, akin to eradicating disease or eliminating poverty," a spokesperson told Fox News Digital at the time. "Her values haven’t changed, but the way she talks about this issue has."

Hong has acknowledged that the governor does not have the power to defund the police.

The candidate brushed off the scrutiny of her posts when asked about them by Fox News Digital ahead of her primary election on Tuesday, saying she wanted to be a sports journalist in college.

"I learned then you have some hot takes, and sometimes bad takes on Twitter, and I let my feelings out into the world," Hong said.

FRANCESCA HONG ASKED ABOUT LACK OF AOC ENDORSEMENT AND THE HOUSE DEM'S REMARK ABOUT THE 'WOKE 1' ERA

She said she was focused on issues voters are concerned about.

Hong's campaign did not return a request for comment on the latest post uncovered by Fox News Digital.

Fox News' CJ Womack and Paul Steinhouser contributed to this report.

item.title: Former Wisconsin Gov Scott Walker warns Hong ‘undermining one of her strengths’ with campaign backtracking
item.description: Former Wisconsin Gov. Scott Walker warns about democratic socialist Francesca Hong's rise as both parties scramble to stop her primary momentum.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE — Former Wisconsin Gov. Scott Walker shared his concerns about politics in the state amid the rise of democratic socialist Francesca Hong, while also arguing she's "undermining" her own campaign in a Fox News Digital interview on Tuesday.

Hong, a Wisconsin state representative, is leading the field heading into Tuesday's Democratic primary, according to recent polling. The far-left, 37-year-old former chef and single mother has courted controversy in recent weeks for her progressive platform and past rhetoric about abolishing the police, as well as her hot take on Thanksgiving.

"Cancel Thanksgiving. Should have done this in 1621," Hong wrote in a now-deleted November 2020 post to X. "If it takes a worldwide pandemic for us to realize we should stop celebrating colonialism and the original superspreader event that killed indigenous folx [sic] and women, so be it," she added. She has since said her views have "evolved," telling Politico Thanksgiving is actually her "favorite" holiday.

"Well one, I think it’s a sign she’ll say just about anything to get elected," Walker, who is now the president of Young America's Foundation, told Fox News Digital ahead of Tuesday’s primary. "And finally, as she’s getting close, thinking she might actually be the nominee, people are telling her you cannot have outrageously outlandish ideas."

WISCONSIN DEM SOCIALIST GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL DODGES WHETHER SHE STILL WANTS TO 'ABOLISH POLICE'

"Not only on Thanksgiving. Doesn’t care for Christmas. Heck, in Wisconsin, doesn’t like Culver’s cheese curds," Walker said, in reference to another of Hong's old social media posts. "Those are all things that are wildly out of touch with the people that she’s going to need if she’s got a shot for the general election."

Walker warned Hong, however, that she could be hurting her campaign because primary voters had been attracted to her, in part, because of her bucking of the Democratic establishment.

"But I think she’s undermining one of her strengths," Walker said. "One of the reasons why she’s going to win today’s primary is because Democratic primary voters view her as not the establishment, not the traditional politician. Someone who will just tell it like it is, even if people don’t agree with her. So the more she backtracks on things she didn’t even say as a kid — she’s actually posted as an elected official — the more I think she starts to undermine her own base, and the typical voter can see right through her." 

Fox News Digital reached out to the Hong campaign for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Walker is the most recent Republican to serve as Wisconsin governor. He was elected in 2010 and 2014 — and also survived a recall in 2012 — before losing to Democrat Tony Evers during a bid for a third term in 2018.

SOCIALIST FRONTRUNNER IN THE HOT SEAT AFTER 'CANCEL THANKSGIVING' POST EMERGES ONLINE

Establishment Democrats have been hoping to stop Hong in her tracks, but she's the clear polling favorite going into Tuesday night. David Crowley, the Milwaukee County executive who earned the endorsement of outgoing Gov. Evers, told Politico that Republicans wanted Hong to be their opponent.

"You know, it’s the only time that I know that the governor — Tony Evers — the Republican Governors Association and Turning Point USA have ever been on the same page: in thinking that Francesca Hong is the best candidate to lose this race," Crowley said.

Whoever wins Tuesday's Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary will face Trump ally Tom Tiffany, who is heavily favored in the Republican primary.

Hong has pushed back on the narrative that she’s too extreme, although she has conspicuously failed to win the endorsement of even far-left darling Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt.

"We have to take this moment, a movement moment, and be bold with transformative change, and build the actual big tent that we can, and we must be as Democrats," Hong told a crowd at a senior community center in Siren.

"It’s common sense versus dangerously crazy," Walker told Fox News Digital of the recent rise of democratic socialism in the U.S. "When you talk about abolishing the police, when you talk about a world without prisons, no consequences for criminals, no push for public safety."

SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM

SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM

Walker said it is intriguing timing that next year will be the 40th anniversary of President Ronald Reagan’s "Tear down this wall" speech at the Berlin Wall.

"In all the years since, I think we’ve kind of lost a sense in America, of why there was a wall there in the first place, why did it have to come down," he said. "That’s because communism and democratic socialism are barriers to freedom. They’re barriers to economic freedom, political freedom, even religious freedom. That’s why Ronald Reagan, Pope John Paul II, Margaret Thatcher and others fought so hard to bring that down. We have to remind anyone, but particularly young people, that democratic socialism has failed in Venezuela, just like communism failed in the old Soviet Union. And it’s a really important reminder."

Walker said the newfound popularity of democratic socialism is in part due to primary voters shifting to the left, particularly under President Donald Trump. Second, he said, is the "years of liberal indoctrination on college campuses." The third, he argued, is due to a strong frustration over housing prices and the feeling that young adults' "piece of the American dream is slipping away," so they are drifting toward the extremes on either side of the aisle.

item.title: Costco employee fatally rammed car into co-worker on motorcycle after seeing hug: DA
item.description: Tyler Sorensen allegedly rammed his car into co-worker Jonathon Langdon's motorcycle in an Issaquah Costco parking lot out of jealousy over a hug.
item.content:encoded:
A Costco employee in a Seattle suburb allegedly rammed his car into a co-worker riding a motorcycle, killing him out of anger and jealousy, according to reports citing statements made to investigators.

Tyler Sorensen, 22, is charged with second-degree murder in connection with the July 31 death of 20-year-old Jonathon Langdon in Issaquah.

Sorensen allegedly followed Langdon out of a Costco parking lot before swerving into his lane and striking his motorcycle, according to court documents obtained by PEOPLE.

SILICON VALLEY DEVELOPER ACCUSED OF MURDER AFTER INVESTIGATORS SAY TESLA REACHED 142 MPH BEFORE FATAL CRASH

Langdon was thrown from his motorcycle into a metal signpost, authorities said. Sorensen fled the scene but returned an hour later with a family member to speak with investigators, according to the Issaquah Police Department.

"The defendant, however, continued on his way without hesitation, only stopping to make sure his vehicle was okay to drive home," states the affidavit obtained by PEOPLE.

Sorensen allegedly told investigators that he became jealous after seeing Langdon hug a female co-worker whom Sorensen claimed was his girlfriend. After seeing the hug, he texted friends that his "blood is boiling."

SEATTLE POLICE CHIEF SNAPS OVER CHICAGO HOME QUESTIONS, ABSENCE FROM CITY AFTER MASS SHOOTING

The female co-worker denied that she and Sorensen had ever dated, stating she had previously told him he was "crossing boundaries," PEOPLE reported.

Sorensen allegedly told law enforcement that his actions were "stupid" and that he only wanted to "spook" Langdon, claiming he did not intend to hit him with his vehicle.

"Our hearts go out to the family and friends of the victim as they process this tragic loss of life," said Issaquah Police Chief Steve Mylett.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the King County Prosecuting Attorney's Office.

item.title: NYPD’s legendary ‘Hip-Hop Cop' Derrick Parker, who investigated rap’s biggest stars and murders, dead at 65
item.description: Derrick Parker, the NYPD's "Hip-Hop Cop" who investigated cases tied to Tupac Shakur, Notorious B.I.G. and Jam Master Jay, has died at age 65.
item.content:encoded:
Derrick Parker, the former NYPD detective known as the "Hip-Hop Cop" for his work in the city's rap-related intelligence unit in the 1990s, has died. He was 65.

His brother, Ralph, told Fox News Digital Monday he died unexpectedly on July 24 at a hospital in New York's Nassau County. He did not give a cause.

A funeral is scheduled for Thursday at the J Foster Phillips Funeral Home in Jamaica, New York.

Derrick J. Parker was the former head of the NYPD's rap intelligence unit when the city's hip-hop scene exploded in popularity in the 1990s. His work included monitoring high-profile artists and their entourages as they came and went from the Big Apple. He said he shared his strategies to reduce violence in the music industry in other parts of the country, including in Miami and Atlanta.

TUPAC SHAKUR MURDER SUSPECT TAKES CENTER STAGE AT TRIAL NEARLY 30 YEARS AFTER SHOOTING SHOCKED MUSIC WORLD

He also served as a homicide and cold case detective during a career that spanned more than 20 years and worked alongside the US Marshals, the ATF, the DEA and the FBI, according to his website.

"You have to watch and see who's coming to your city. Who's there and who's what," he told Fox News Digital in a 2024 interview. "We can't track everybody, but when certain people come to the city, you should know who, especially certain people that are on your radar. That's the way I look at it."

Much of the job, he said, involved keeping law enforcement and nightclub management aware of who was going where in order to avoid potential confrontations between rival groups.

CASSIE VENTURA FLED THE UNITED STATES AFTER TESTIFYING AGAINST DIDDY IN SEX CRIMES TRIAL: DOCS

He played a role in the 1999 investigation into the Club New York shooting where music mogul Sean "Diddy" Combs was charged but later acquitted. Pop superstar Jennifer Lopez was also briefly detained and released.

Parker said his approach to policing the hip-hop world wasn't to come down hard on its stars.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"I was the law, so he was always friendly," he later said of Combs. "I'm never hard on these guys. They know what they get into. They know what trouble they have."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

Parker wrote a book about his experiences, "Notorious C.O.P.: The Inside Story of the Tupac, Biggie and Jam Master Jay Investigations from the NYPD's First 'Hip-Hop Cop.'" The book chronicled his involvement in investigations surrounding three of hip-hop's most notorious killings: Tupac Shakur, Christopher Wallace, who performed as the Notorious B.I.G. and Jam Master Jay, the Run-DMC DJ whose real name was Jason Mizell.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

It would be decades before Mizell's killers went on trial. Parker was on the witness stand.

After Parker retired from the NYPD in 2002, he worked in security for large events and executive protection applying the same philosophy of knowing who would be going where to avoid conflicts.

He also became a frequent media commentator on high-profile cases involving figures and venues he had encountered during his NYPD career, including Combs' sex-trafficking trial last year and even the wedding between Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce at Madison Square Garden.

GOT A TIP?

He had also told Fox News Digital that he hoped to write a follow-up book.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"I want to really tell a big, big story about a lot of stuff," he said.

Days before his death, he said he was closely following the Las Vegas murder case against Duane "Keffe D" Davis, who is charged with playing a role in Tupac Shakur's 1996 murder. Jury selection began Monday.

"We were supposed to go out to dinner for my birthday," Ralph Parker told Fox News Digital. "He's like, ‘Oh, we're gonna go out and eat. Your birthday's coming, don't worry about it.’ Well, I won't be able to go eat with him."

item.title: Veteran lifeguard, 71, dragged underwater off the coast of Maine by great white shark
item.description: Greg Wilfert, a 71-year-old lifeguard at Scarborough Beach for 55 years, was dragged underwater by a great white shark while swimming near buoys.
item.content:encoded:
A 71-year-old lifeguard and park manager in Maine had an encounter with a great white shark off the coast over the weekend. He initially thought his rescue can got caught on a boat after he was dragged underwater.

But it wasn’t a boat. Greg Wilfert, who has worked at Scarborough Beach for 55 years and looks like a guy who should have his own reality show, was pulled five to six feet under the water by a great white.

He was swimming around the buoys at the time with a few other lifeguards. Luckily, he was able to remove the strap from the rescue device then swim back to shore to safety without any further interactions with the shark.

SHARK WEEK SHOCKER AS GREAT WHITE BREACHES JUST YARDS FROM OBLIVIOUS BOOGIE BOARDER

"I thought a boat had come by and grabbed my rescue can because I got pulled under, and I realized right away that it was not a boat, that it had to have been a great white," Wilfert told WHDH.

"I just swam as fast as I could to the surface, and then I just was hoping it wasn't behind me. I could've beaten Michael Phelps."

Once he made it back to shore, his duty as a lifeguard took over. He warned the beachgoers, had them get out of the water, then shut down the beach for an hour.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

FISHING CONTENT CREATOR WHO FILMED HIMSELF BEING BITTEN BY A SHARK WHILE SPEARFISHING LUCKY HE STILL HAS LEG

Since his encounter, Wilfert has had jet skis and drones keeping an eye on the water for other great white sharks. While he wasn’t hurt, he is taking his encounter seriously.

There's been an increase in great white activity in the area recently and this veteran of the beach isn't taking any chances.

"There's a lot of beaches that we have around here that there's no lifeguards, and they have the presence of these great whites, and you need to take it seriously," he said.

"I'm taking it seriously. I won't be swimming the buoys for a while."

item.title: Elite rock climber's cause of death revealed after horrific accident at national park
item.description: Rock climber Jake Whisenant died from blunt force trauma in a fall at Sequoia National Park, authorities confirmed. The elite climber set records on El Capitan.
item.content:encoded:
Authorities have revealed the cause of death of Jake Whisenant, an elite rock climber who recently died in an accident in California's Sierra Nevada, shocking many. 

Whisenant died of "blunt force trauma injuries, sustained as a result of a fall," the Tulare County Sheriff’s Office told Fox News Digital. He was just 30 years old.

The spokesperson also disclosed that the incident took place at Sequoia National Park.

RECORD-SETTING EL CAPITAN ROCK CLIMBER DIES AT AGE 30 IN SIERRA NEVADA ACCIDENT

Whisenant’s death was first announced by his friend, Bailee Moore, who remembered him as her "lifelong friend and confidant."

"Our family is absolutely devastated by this news but find solace in the fact that Jake died doing what he loves in the beautiful Sierra Nevada," said Moore.

"I will look for you in every life, my brother. Now go rest high up on that mountain."

Whisenant had established himself in Yosemite's climbing community through a series of impressive feats on El Capitan, one of the world’s most challenging rock-climbing destinations, as Fox News Digital previously reported. 

NURSE IMPALED BY POLE DURING HIKE FORCED TO TREK 10 MILES FOR HELP: 'A FREAK THING'

In May, Whisenant teamed up with fellow climber Noah Fox to climb El Capitan's Nose route twice in one day, completing the feat in 14 hours and 38 minutes, according to the Yosemite Climbing Association.

In October 2024, Whisenant and another climber named Brant Hysell set a speed record on El Capitan's Lurking Fear route, completing the climb in 2 hours, 55 minutes and 32 seconds.

At the time, Whisenant described it as a "truly magical day that I’ll never forget."

YELLOWSTONE OFFICIALS DECIDE FATE OF BISON THAT LAUNCHED GRANDFATHER 8 FEET IN AIR

"We both tapped into a flow state, fully committed to our plan, and most importantly had an absolute blast on our favorite rock," he wrote on Instagram.

It takes an "incredible commitment" to excel at climbing, Michael Gervais, a high-performance psychologist and founder of Finding Mastery, said in an interview with Fox News Digital.

Gervais, based in California, said becoming an elite climber requires an extraordinary level of mental and physical commitment. (He did not advise or work with Whisenant.)

"The consequences are so high, because the thrill is so wonderful," said Gervais. "It requires an all-in full commitment to be elite in this consequential sport."

"They’re able to override that reflexive brain dictum and focus all their attention on the task at hand: the next placehold, the next foothold, the next challenge in front of them to be able to solve," added Gervais.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"That type of incredible psychological and technical skill is rare, and it is special."

He cautioned against viewing elite climbers as thrill-seekers or "adrenaline junkies."

"From the inside, spending the last 25 years working with the best athletes in the world ... we have a very different perspective," said Gervais.

"Elite climbers, in this case — they are not adrenaline junkies. They have developed the full capacity to become incredibly present in environments where full command of themselves is required," he added.

"So, it's that state of being fully present that I think is incredibly compelling."

item.title: HHS bureaucrats accused of 'sabotaging' RFK Jr's efforts to expose Fauci records
item.description: Sen. Ron Johnson alleges career bureaucrats within HHS are sabotaging efforts to uncover pandemic-era information from Anthony Fauci's government iPhone.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: A Senate Republican leading a dive into Dr. Anthony Fauci’s old government iPhone alleged that "career bureaucrats" within Fauci’s old agency are sabotaging the senator’s and others’ quest for information from the pandemic era.

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., told Fox News Digital that he believed longtime employees of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) were putting up roadblocks to his own probe and other information trawling expeditions pushed by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

"Again, we don't know what we don’t know," Johnson said. "We don't know what HHS has. Bobby Kennedy doesn't know what HHS has."

FAUCI HELD IN CONTEMPT AS COVID CELLPHONE LANDS IN HANDS OF SENATE INVESTIGATORS

Johnson, along with Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., received a copy of Fauci’s personal work phone from HHS as part of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee’s broader investigation into the former head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID). 

On Monday, Johnson’s panel, the Senate Homeland Security Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, released the first tranche of private messages found on the device, which included over 34,000 text messages and 522 voicemails.

The first batch of texts, exchanged between Fauci and former Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Director Dr. Rochelle Walensky and Dr. Vivek Murthy, who would become surgeon general under the Biden administration, revealed that Fauci had concerns about the effects of the second dose of mRNA vaccines on pregnant women in the first trimester.

FAUCI'S HHS IPHONE TURNED OVER TO SENATE INVESTIGATORS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

"I asked around a bit more and another issue came up that you need to be aware of," Fauci wrote. "Since many people have significant cytokines storm and fever after the 2nd dose, this theoretically could be associated with miscarriage in the 1st trimester."

The lawmaker believed that the revelation was just the "tip of the iceberg," but has remained cautious with his investigation and what information dumps come next, particularly to protect the personal information of others who may be included in the communications.

FAUCI IN THE HOT SEAT AS GOP SENATOR TEARS INTO 'TRULY SICK' VACCINE TEXTS: 'TIP OF THE ICEBERG'

He argued that releasing the first batch of texts was based on public health and safety concerns, said that Fauci’s concern "immediately impacts public safety, immediately impacts informed consent."

As he waded through the rest of the information on the phone, Johnson believed that there was more to find about the HHS’ handling of the COVID-19 pandemic, and charged that even though Kennedy was at the helm, not even he had full knowledge of the information that could be lurking within the agency.

"I mean, fortunately, now we have Bobby Kennedy, I think gaining a little bit more control over the agency," Johnson said. "Remember, most of the people serving in these agencies have been there a long time, and they were involved in the cover-up. They were supposed to be surveilling for vaccine injuries and they weren’t."

"So, you know, Bobby Kennedy has people in those agencies sabotaging his efforts at radical transparency," he continued. "So this is like pulling teeth. So, I mean, I did not know they had government-issued phones. They've been sitting there, locked away somewhere."

HHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Dangerous drug-resistant fungus spreads across US, reaching 27 states
item.description: Thousands of Candida auris cases have been reported across 27 states in 2026, with the drug-resistant fungus posing deadly risks in healthcare settings.
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of cases of a potentially deadly, drug-resistant fungus have been reported across 27 states so far this year, according to provisional CDC data.

As of the week ending July 25, a total of 3,437 clinical cases of Candida auris (C. auris) had been documented in the U.S. so far in 2026.

California accounts for 873 cases — roughly one-quarter of the country’s total. Other states with high numbers include Texas (433), Tennessee (283), Ohio (279), Georgia (193), Louisiana (179), Illinois (171), Arizona (171), Michigan (146), Virginia (132) and Pennsylvania (121), per the CDC.

EXPERTS REVEAL HOW TO AVOID DEADLY LEGIONNAIRES' DISEASE AS NYC OUTBREAK KILLS 5

The remaining states have fewer than 100 cases each.

Candida auris is a type of yeast that can cause serious infections, primarily in hospitals, nursing homes and other healthcare settings.

The fungus, which can survive on surfaces for prolonged periods, is "highly transmissible between patients through contact with contaminated surfaces or objects," the CDC states. It can spread through contaminated items such as bedrails, doorknobs and shared medical equipment.

C. auris can also be spread by people who carry the fungus but do not show symptoms, known as "colonization."

Clinical cases do not necessarily represent infections. The CDC defines a clinical case as detection of C. auris in a specimen collected during the normal course of medical care. 

Some clinical specimens can come from sites where the presence of C. auris may represent colonization rather than a true infection.

The health effects of the fungus can range from colonization without symptoms to potentially deadly invasive infections, including bloodstream infections.

Those most at risk of infection include patients with severe underlying medical conditions. In particular, those who use breathing tubes, feeding tubes, IVs or catheters are more vulnerable, as are those who are hospitalized frequently or for long periods of time.

People without those risk factors are unlikely to become colonized with C. auris or develop an infection.

Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst and clinical professor of medicine at NYU Langone, said he considers C. auris an "emerging problem of great concern."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"It is resistant to multiple antifungal drugs, and it tends to spread in hospital settings, including on equipment being used on immunocompromised and semi-immunocompromised patients, such as ventilators and catheters," he previously told Fox News Digital.

"Unfortunately, symptoms such as fever, chills and aches may be ubiquitous, and it can be mistaken for other infections."

Invasive C. auris infections have been associated with mortality rates of 30% to 72%, although most affected patients are already seriously ill. This can make it difficult to determine how often the fungus is a direct cause of death.

Candida auris can be difficult to treat because it is often resistant to antifungal medications, leading the CDC to classify the fungus as an "urgent antimicrobial-resistance threat."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

More than 90% of U.S. samples are resistant to fluconazole, a common antifungal treatment. Echinocandins, another family of antifungals, are currently the main treatment option for C. auris, although some strains are resistant to all three main classes of antifungals.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"Major research" is ongoing to develop new treatments, according to Siegel.

"This is part of a much larger problem of emerging antibiotic resistance in the U.S. and around the world," the physician previously cautioned. "At the same time, sterilization and disinfection measures in hospitals can be very helpful."

Fox News Digital's Angelica Stabile contributed reporting.

item.title: 2 custodians dead in possible murder-suicide at Chicago elementary school
item.description: Two custodians were found dead from gunshot wounds inside Mark Twain Elementary School in Chicago when no students were present in the building.
item.content:encoded:
Two custodians were found shot to death Monday inside a Chicago elementary school after one of them allegedly killed his co-worker before turning the weapon on himself, according to reports.

A 48-year-old woman and a 63-year-old man were found unresponsive inside Mark Twain Elementary School just after 3:30 p.m., the Chicago Police Department said.

Both were shot once in the head, authorities said. They were taken to local hospitals, where they were pronounced dead.

TWO FOUND SHOT TO DEATH INSIDE CAR ON UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO CAMPUS: REPORT

An unspecified weapon was found at the scene.

School principal Matthew Moline confirmed the deaths in a letter to parents, WTTW-TV reported. He said shots were fired inside the building at a time when no students were present.

"I am sorry to share that members of our school community were impacted," he wrote.

SEIU Local 73, the union that represents Chicago Public Schools custodial employees, confirmed both unidentified victims worked at the elementary school.

DISPATCH AUDIO RELEASED IN MICHIGAN FAMILY MURDER-SUICIDE AS TROUBLED FAMILY'S SECRETS EMERGE

"The only facts we know right now are that two families have lost a loved one and our prayers are with their families, and the staff, students, and families at Mark Twain Elementary School," SEIU Local 73 Executive Vice President Trumaine Reeves said in a statement.

The older custodian was upset that he was slated to be transferred from the school, the Chicago Sun-Times reported, citing a police report. He allegedly shot his co-worker before shooting himself, according to the newspaper.

"We know that this news will be deeply concerning to our families and staff," Moline wrote in his letter. "We will work to provide additional information to the school community as the investigation proceeds."

Fox News Digital has reached out to the police department, Chicago Public Schools, and Moline, the school principal.

item.title: Vikings quarterback battle meets expected end as Kyler Murray beats out JJ McCarthy for starting job
item.description: Kyler Murray wins the Minnesota Vikings quarterback battle over J.J. McCarthy, but multiple accounts say the veteran has struggled at times in camp.
item.content:encoded:
If two quarterbacks who have been inconsistent in their careers and inconsistent in practice despite moments of clarity need to settle the battle for the starting job, what does an NFL franchise do in picking one? The Minnesota Vikings answered that on Tuesday by picking Kyler Murray.

Minnesota coach Kevin O'Connell has named Kyler Murray his starting quarterback, the club announced.

A Vikings source told Fox News Digital/OutKick that picking Murray over third-year veteran J.J. McCarthy was the expectation even before Tuesday's decision.

Yes, this was predictable.

VIKINGS SIGNING KYLER MURRAY MAKES J.J. MCCARTHY ODD MAN OUT

The sources pointed to Murray's greater experience in his eighth NFL season as a major factor in separating him from the younger McCarthy.

This is not good news for McCarthy. The No. 10 pick of the 2024 draft, he is now sidelined at a time in his career when most first-rounders are expected to blossom as veterans.

McCarthy, who missed his rookie year with a knee injury, has only 10 NFL starts and that inability to hold the starting job and beat out Murray raises questions about his future.

The Vikings may decide McCarthy is a valuable trade commodity because they also have Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer on the roster.

Murray, who has been splitting first-team practice repetitions with McCarthy throughout the offseason and at the start of training camp, can now move forward as not only the team's clear starter but leader.

He apparently could use as much work with the starters on offense as he can get in the month that remains before the regular-season opener because Murray has by multiple accounts, struggled at times in recent weeks.

He got that by beating out McCarthy once news of the rookie's injury came to light. And he went on to have a great season and eventually signed with the Seattle Seahawks before leading them to the Super Bowl title last season.

If you've started shopping for a VPN, you've probably come across the terms shared IP and dedicated IP. While they may sound technical, the difference is actually pretty straightforward, and choosing the right one can make your online experience smoother.

Both options encrypt your internet traffic and protect your connection, but they serve different purposes. One prioritizes maximum privacy by blending your activity with thousands of other users. The other gives you your own personal IP address, making it easier to access certain online services without additional verification.

Here's what each option does, and how to decide which one is right for you.

A shared IP is exactly what it sounds like: multiple VPN users connect through the same public IP address. When dozens, or even hundreds, of people are using the same IP at different times, it becomes much harder for websites or other observers to associate online activity with any one individual. That's one reason shared IPs are the default choice for most VPN services.

The trade-off is that shared IPs can sometimes trigger CAPTCHAs, blocked logins or extra verification if a website sees too much activity coming from the same address. That is one reason some people look for ways to fix a VPN that keeps getting blocked.

A dedicated IP is reserved exclusively for you. No one else using the VPN service shares that IP address. Because your IP remains consistent every time you connect, websites and online services recognize it as the same connection. That can make certain activities more convenient, especially if you regularly access accounts that use IP-based security checks.

For example, some businesses only allow employees to log in from approved IP addresses. Using a dedicated IP allows your company to "whitelist" this IP so that you can log in smoothly every time.

A dedicated IP can also reduce the number of verification requests you receive when signing in to banking websites, business software, or other accounts that flag unfamiliar locations. If you've ever been annoyed by a CAPTCHA (e.g., "which one of these photos is of a motorcycle?") when trying to log in from a new location, you'll appreciate the consistency of a dedicated IP address.

Some people might argue that letting your VPN provider assign you a dedicated IP inherently makes you less private. This is where your choice of VPN provider is important. A reputable VPN provider distributes IP addresses with a zero-knowledge allocation system, meaning not even the provider can trace it back to you.

With this kind of dedicated IP, you still receive the privacy and encryption benefits of a VPN; the difference is simply that your VPN IP belongs only to you.

The answer depends on how you use the internet. A shared IP is usually the better option if your main goals are privacy, anonymous browsing, and protecting your data while traveling or using public Wi-Fi. Since many people are using the same address, your online activity is more difficult to distinguish from everyone else's.

A dedicated IP makes sense if convenience is your priority. If you frequently work remotely, access company resources with IP restrictions, manage servers remotely, or want fewer login challenges from websites that recognize your connection, having your own VPN IP can save time. Neither option is inherently more secure than the other. Both encrypt your internet traffic and hide your original IP address from the websites you visit. The main difference is whether you want to share your VPN identity with other users or have one reserved just for yourself.

A strong VPN should use modern encryption, follow a verified no-logs policy and include a kill switch that blocks internet traffic if the VPN connection drops. It should also work across iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac and compatible routers.

Look for a provider with servers in many countries, support for streaming and secure browsing, multiple simultaneous device connections and responsive customer support. A money-back guarantee can also give you time to test its speed, reliability and ease of use before committing.

Both shared and dedicated VPN IP addresses offer the core benefits people expect from a VPN: encrypted internet traffic, improved online privacy, and protection on public networks. The right choice comes down to how you use the internet. For most people, a shared IP provides the best balance of privacy and simplicity. If you need a consistent online identity for work, secure logins, or specialized services, a dedicated IP may be worth considering. item.title: NBA appears to prioritize European audience with announcement of unique 2026-27 season opener
item.description: The 2026-27 NBA regular season tips off with the Detroit Pistons hosting Boston Celtics at 3 PM ET, a move likely aimed at European viewership growth.
item.content:encoded:
The NBA is a global league.

That is a statement that basketball fans have heard countless times, especially since Adam Silver took over as the league's commissioner in 2014, but we have perhaps never seen an announcement by the NBA that better represents that statement than the one the league made on Tuesday.

The league shared the news that the 2026-27 NBA regular season will get underway on Tuesday, Oct. 20, with the Detroit Pistons playing host to the Boston Celtics. Two historic Eastern Conference foes tipping off a new season, with the presumption of a marquee matchup to follow the same evening, would be a standard move for the league.

That is the case here with the Philadelphia 76ers and New York Knicks and the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs following the opener on Tuesday, but there is one very important detail to note: the Celtics-Pistons game will tip off at 3 p.m. ET.

Celebrating the start of a new NBA season on a Tuesday afternoon when the majority of the league's North American fanbase will be working seems like a bizarre decision. One, and perhaps the only explanation here, is that the league's season-opening decision doesn't actually have fans in North America at the top of mind.

The NBA appeasing its fans across Europe would make sense following the viewership explosion from fans across the pond a season ago.

The 2025-26 NBA season marked the first of the league's 11-year media deal with Disney, NBCUniversal, and Amazon Prime, with Prime confirming that its coverage of the league outside of the U.S. was up 28% year-over-year.

According to SVG Europe, viewership of NBA games on Prime across Europe was up 129% year-over-year versus the previous season. The NBA Finals saw an uptick of 130% compared to the previous season across Europe.

item.title: Sherrill drops head-turning voter ID declaration in wake of registration fiasco: ‘Significant shift’
item.description: Gov. Mikie Sherrill says she would support voter ID in New Jersey, even as she blasts the federal SAVE Act that Donald Trump champions as suppression.
item.content:encoded:
New Jersey Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill says she would support a voter ID law in the Garden State — even as she slams President Donald Trump’s federal SAVE Act push as "voter suppression."

"Governor Sherrill supports the current rules requiring ID for voter registration and she is open to considering proposals to strengthen those to make sure we have the strongest, fairest elections in the nation," a spokesperson in the governor's office told Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

Sherrill’s comments hand New Jersey Republicans a new opening to press Democrats on voter ID, even as she rejects Trump’s broader federal election push under the SAVE America Act.

Sherrill's office responded to Fox News Digital on Tuesday after the Garden State Democrat told local media in July she would support a voter ID law if one were passed in New Jersey, saying she "doesn't have a problem with voter ID."

SCHUMER SAID ‘DEMOCRATS SUPPORT VOTER ID’ — THEN EVERY SENATE DEMOCRAT VOTED AGAINST GOP BILL

"I’m very opposed to the SAVE Act," Sherrill added at the time. "I do believe that is just a tool of voter suppression and an attempt to get all of the personal identifying information of New Jerseyans into the federal government systems, which I’m opposed to."

Sherrill served in the House for seven years and voted against the SAVE Act in 2025, with her office describing the measure as an "extreme voter suppression bill."

Sherrill is facing criticism after announcing last month that a Motor Vehicle Commission system error improperly registered roughly 6,600 people who had indicated they were not U.S. citizens. The state said fewer than 400 people newly registered because of the error voted, and later announced that more than 4,500 registrations were being removed while the remaining cases undergo additional review because some of those individuals may be citizens.

New Jersey Assembly Minority Leader John DiMaio told Fox News Digital Sherrill's recent comments mark a "significant shift" after years of Republicans in the Garden State advocating for voter ID.

NEW JERSEY REMOVES 6,600 PEOPLE FROM VOTER ROLLS WHO WERE ELIGIBLE TO CAST A BALLOT FOR 2024 ELECTION

"But agreeing with us publicly is the easy part," DiMaio said, adding that Democratic legislative leaders control what gets a hearing and a vote, and that Republicans have so far heard nothing from them on voter ID.

"We’ve been pushing voter ID and other election integrity reforms for years. The bills are already introduced. We’ve repeatedly called for hearings and votes. The roadblock has been Democratic legislative leadership," the Republican state leader said.

DiMaio said the Motor Vehicle System failure exposed serious weaknesses in New Jersey’s election safeguards and they still have not heard an answer of what went wrong.

Voter-ID requirements have repeatedly become major partisan fights at the state level, with Democrats and voting-rights groups arguing that some requirements can make it harder for eligible voters to cast ballots.

One of the most prominent battles erupted in Georgia in 2021. The state already required photo ID for in-person voting, but a sweeping Republican-backed election law added identification requirements for absentee voting along with other changes. The backlash went national, with MLB moving its 2021 All-Star Game out of Atlanta and some Hollywood figures threatening boycotts.

HARRIS BECOMES ACCIDENTAL SAVE ACT ‘SALESWOMAN’ AS TRUMP ATTACK SPECTACULARLY BACKFIRES

"Governor Sherrill served our country in the military and as a public servant because she believes in every citizen's right to participate in our democracy by voting. That's why she has stood firm against MAGA Republicans' voter suppression attempts and Trump’s demands for New Jersey voters’ personal identifiable information," said a spokesperson in the office of the governor.

"She has already made voting more accessible by signing the John R. Lewis Voter Empowerment Act and expanded early voting in municipal elections," the spokesperson added, referencing the law that bans voter intimidation and discrimination, expanding language assistance, and requiring extra review of election changes in places with a history of discrimination.

Trump has continued to prioritize and highlight the issue of noncitizens on voter rolls as he renewed his push for the SAVE America Act, which would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register for federal elections and photo identification to cast a federal ballot.

"I think they should pass Voter I.D. I think they should pass proof of citizenship—basically SAVE America Act... I think that should be something that we should absolutely get," Trump said in the Oval Office Monday.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment.

item.title: Stephen A. Smith blames ‘the right’ for WNBA firestorm, says league ‘left the door open’
item.description: Stephen A. Smith blames the WNBA league office for failing to set clear transgender eligibility rules, arguing it opened the door for political opponents.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN host Stephen A. Smith tried to pin some of the political turmoil surrounding the WNBA on "the right," but his argument ultimately circled back to the league's own failures.

Even as Smith accused conservatives of politicizing controversy, he argued that the WNBA created the opening by failing to establish clear rules and leadership, namely around the transgender issue increasingly confronting the league.

On his eponymous YouTube show Monday, Smith put the responsibility on the league office, arguing that its lack of clear guidelines has allowed disputes over biological males competing in women's sports to consume the conversation.

THE WNBA HAS LIMITED OPTIONS AFTER TWO MEN DECLARED FOR THE DRAFT, AND THOSE OPTIONS AREN'T GREAT

"You’ve got to have rules and regulations," Smith said. "You’ve got to have law. You’ve got to have order. You can’t have this."

Smith then turned his attention to the right, accusing conservatives of maneuvering through the controversy for political advantage.

That includes former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White, who have declared themselves eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft in an effort to challenge the league's gender-eligibility rules.

Smith's larger point: The WNBA left the door open for its political opponents to walk right through it.

FORMER NBA STAR ENES KANTER FREEDOM WRITES LETTER TO WNBA OFFICIALLY DECLARING FOR 2027 DRAFT

"Sure, the right is maneuvering its way through the terrain and politicizing this issue," Smith said. "It doesn’t negate the fact that the WNBA left the door open for it to happen. They have dropped the ball. I’m talking about the league office. I’m not talking about players."

Smith blamed the right for exploiting the controversy while simultaneously arguing that the WNBA made itself vulnerable to that exploitation.

"And now it’s gotten to the point where everything about them is going to be politicized."

Smith brought up Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who has drawn attention for speaking out on women's sports and has taken plenty of heat for views that don't exactly mesh with the WNBA establishment.

WHITE HOUSE DEFENDS WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AFTER SHE SPEAKS OUT IN SUPPORT OF PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS

Smith pointed to Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier and questioned whether the Republican official would show the same interest if an athlete expressed liberal views. Smith also made clear that he agrees with Cunningham's position on protecting female athletics.

"You’ve got the Florida attorney general. Clearly, it’s politicized. I wonder if he would have said that if it was somebody other than Sophie Cunningham, who obviously has made a name for herself speaking up about the issues that she has spoken about as it pertains to protecting girls in competitive sports, which, by the way, I support her position on," Smith said.

"If that had been a liberal, or somebody with a liberal-thinking mind in terms of that particular issue, who spouted stuff opposite of what Sophie Cunningham would have said, would the Florida attorney general, James Uthmeier, have taken that position then? I don’t think so, but I don’t know."

But Smith's attempt to blame the right for politicizing the controversy also served his broader criticism of the WNBA.

"But the time has come for folks to stop whining about how stuff is being politicized and do something about it so it can’t be politicized," Smith said. "Do something or suck it up! Do something or suck it up. You don’t have a choice other than those two."

Smith closed with a warning: As long as the WNBA keeps serving up perceived double standards, critics will keep feasting on them.

"You’ve got to take a stand at some point, because folks are coming," Smith said. "Because it’s an opportunity to point out flagrant hypocrisies, and they’re not going to pass it up, no matter what folks say."

item.title: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens backs El-Sayed after narrow primary defeat, calls socialism ‘dangerous’
item.description: Michigan Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens defends endorsing Abdul El-Sayed after their Senate primary, reaffirming her identity as a "Zionist Democrat."
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens rallied behind former opponent Abdul El-Sayed following her narrow Senate primary defeat last week, casting the decision as a matter of accepting the will of Democratic voters despite their political differences.

"That's called democracy," Stevens said while defending her endorsement on Tuesday.

"You don't sign up for a Democratic Party to be salty grapes and... just continue to hold a grudge," she added.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

Stevens, who was viewed as the more moderate of the Democrats vying to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters, spent the primary drawing contrasts with El-Sayed on issues ranging from Israel to the direction of the Democratic Party.

Those differences haven't disappeared with the primary.

During an appearance on "America's Newsroom," Stevens reaffirmed her identity as a "Zionist Democrat" while acknowledging that candidates who share her politics haven't been faring as well in Democratic primaries.

"I believe in democracy. He won the majority of the votes, and I'm going to continue to stand by my positions," she told co-anchor Bill Hemmer.

LEFT-WING ACTIVISTS HECKLE PRO-ISRAEL DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS AT MICHIGAN CONVENTION

"I'm a Zionist Democrat. I am a Democrat who gets endorsed by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the AFL-CIO. I have been recognized over and over again as one of our most effective lawmakers. I identify problems and I solve them... I'm a patriot. I love our freedoms. I love this country and, yes, I am still in the Democratic Party, even though folks like me maybe aren't winning our primaries."

El-Sayed, meanwhile, has emerged as a prominent figure on the party's progressive flank.

While he rejects the "socialist" label, El-Sayed backs several progressive policies, including abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), ending U.S. military aid to Israel and establishing Medicare for all.

Stevens also drew a clear distinction between her former opponent and socialism, noting that her former rival had rejected the label before offering her own assessment of the ideology.

"My Democratic opponent, now the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan, has disavowed socialism. I think we all should. It's dangerous," she said.

She went on to identify herself as a "proud... Democratic labor capitalist" who had made that aspect of her identity a tenet of her campaign.

item.title: Trump cheers Alito staying for another Supreme Court term: 'One of the greatest of all time'
item.description: President Donald Trump praised Associate Justice Samuel Alito's decision to stay on the U.S. Supreme Court in a social media post on Truth Social.
item.content:encoded:
In a late-night social media post, President Donald Trump celebrated Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito's decision to remain on the bench for another term.

Trump’s celebration of the 76-year-old conservative stalwart’s decision to put off retirement comes as the midterms raise the stakes over how long Republicans will retain the Senate majority needed to confirm any eventual successor.

"Great news for our Country! Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito has announced that he is staying for another Term," Trump wrote Monday night on Truth Social. "He is one of the Greatest of All Time. We are all lucky!"

Alito confirmed last week that he plans to remain on the nation's highest court for its coming term, batting down months of speculation that he could retire while Trump is in the White House and Republicans still control the Senate.

ALITO NOT EXPECTED TO RETIRE THIS TERM, COOLING SUPREME COURT VACANCY SPECULATION: SOURCES

"Obviously, I'm here for another term," Alito said in an interview published by The Wall Street Journal.

The Supreme Court’s next term begins in October and typically concludes with its final opinions in late June or early July. The justices are currently on their summer recess.

Alito and fellow conservative Justice Clarence Thomas, 78, have faced some calls from conservatives to step down, which would give Trump one potential last chance to appoint a fourth Supreme Court justice to the lifetime post.

Trump appointed three others during his first term in office – Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh and Amy Coney Barrett – giving the court a 6-3 conservative majority that has issued a series of major rulings since 2020.

"It's not pleasant, in the sense that it's a reminder of mortality," Alito told the Journal about the calls to retire. "It's like, what are those vultures doing up there? They are flying around. But it goes with life tenure."

TRUMP REVEALS HE HAS MULTI-PICK SCOTUS PLAN READY AS RETIREMENT SPECULATION HEATS UP

The window to replace one of the court's oldest conservative justices with a younger jurist who could potentially remain on the bench for decades might narrow considerably after November.

Republicans currently hold a 53-47 Senate advantage, counting the two independents who caucus with Democrats on the Democratic side. Because Supreme Court nominees require Senate confirmation, a Democratic takeover in the 2026 midterms could effectively prevent Trump from replacing Alito — or any other justice — with a nominee opposed by a unified Democratic majority.

Democrats would need a net gain of four seats to reach 51 and take outright control, with Republican Vice President JD Vance otherwise positioned to break a 50-50 tie.

That reality places unusual weight on Alito's decision to remain.

Alito was born April 1, 1950, making him 76, and has served on the Supreme Court since January 2006 after being nominated by President George W. Bush. He is one of the court's most consistently conservative members.

The court has disclosed relatively little about Alito's health over the years, signaling he remains in good health. Alito did have a minor incident while attending a Federalist Society event in Philadelphia on March 20, being treated for dehydration after his security detail urged him to see a doctor rather than make the roughly three-hour drive home.

He was released that night, was subsequently examined by his physician and returned to work the following Monday.

NPR RETRACTS FALSE REPORT CLAIMING JUSTICE SAMUEL ALITO IS RETIRING FROM THE SUPREME COURT

Questions about Alito’s longevity on the bench and decision to stay introduces another potential inflection point: the 2028 presidential election.

If the White House changes parties in 2028, Alito remaining beyond Trump’s term carries the risk for conservatives that a future Democratic president could nominate his successor the following January.

That outcome is far from predetermined, and subject to whatever party controls the Senate, but the modern political era has repeatedly seen the White House swing between parties.

In six of the seven elections since 1988 that produced a new president, control of the presidency also changed parties — the lone exception being Republican George H.W. Bush's victory after Ronald Reagan in 1988. That run includes the succession from Bush to Bill Clinton, George W. Bush, Barack Obama, Trump, Joe Biden and back to Trump.

For Trump, the stakes surrounding an aging Supreme Court justice are hardly theoretical.

He confronted perhaps the most consequential Supreme Court vacancy of his first presidency on Sept. 18, 2020, when reporters informed him on an airport tarmac after a campaign rally in Bemidji, Minnesota, that liberal Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg had died.

TRUMP PRAISES LINDSEY GRAHAM AS SENATOR WHOSE KAVANAUGH FIGHT CHANGED SUPREME COURT HISTORY

"She just died? Wow. I didn't know that," Trump said before praising Ginsburg as an "amazing woman" who had led an "amazing life."

The timing immediately transformed the final weeks of the 2020 presidential campaign.

Trump moved quickly to select then-Judge Amy Coney Barrett to replace Ginsburg – just eight days after her death – and the Republican-controlled Senate confirmed Barrett on Oct. 26, 2020, by a 52-48 vote, just 27 days after her nomination, eight days before Election Day.

Landing three new justices during a single four-year presidential term was a historically rare achievement. Not since Richard Nixon's first term had a president placed at least three new members on the Supreme Court in one term. Nixon ultimately placed four — Warren Burger, Harry Blackmun, Lewis Powell and William Rehnquist — on the court before beginning his second term.

Trump's three appointments have continued to shape some of the most consequential rulings of his second administration, making the future of Alito's seat particularly significant for both parties.

For now, Alito has made his choice to stay active, with Trump is cheering him on.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Francesca Hong asked about lack of AOC endorsement and the House Dem's remark about the 'Woke 1' era
item.description: Wisconsin state Rep. Francesca Hong, who is running in the Democratic gubernatorial primary, was asked about U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's "Woke 1" comment.
item.content:encoded:
Wisconsin Democratic socialist gubernatorial primary candidate Francesca Hong fielded questions on Monday pertaining to progressive U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., who did not endorse Hong in Tuesday's primary contest.

Asked why she thinks the congresswoman — who is often referred to simply by her initials AOC — and U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., did not back her, Hong said, "I have so much respect for the senator and the congresswoman, and they are working tirelessly to make sure that we can flip Congress and the Senate and get Democrats wins in the midterms. I look forward to conversations with them about that too."

Pressed on whether she believes the two lawmakers not endorsing her signals they don't believe she can win the state, Hong said that a gubernatorial contest "is different from federal elections."

WISCONSIN PROGRESSIVE HONG'S SUPPORTERS ARE CONFIDENT SHE'S THE ANSWER TO AFFORDABILITY AHEAD OF PRIMARY

During a Sunday interview on ABC's "This Week," Jonathan Karl asked Ocasio-Cortez whether she would endorse Hong.

SOCIALIST FRONTRUNNER IN THE HOT SEAT AFTER 'CANCEL THANKSGIVING' POST EMERGES ONLINE

"And I have a local city councilman that has this... saying, 'Woke 1 was crazy,'" she said, laughing. "And I think that what's important is that we have to assess what a candidate is saying now."

When asked on Monday about Ocasio-Cortez's wokeness-related comment, Hong, a Democratic Socialists of America member, suggested that individuals "are opening their eyes to an economy that is deeply rigged against working-class people" and that she will speak about how to "deliver for working class people by taxing the ultrarich, ensure that we have a moratorium on data centers, that we're raising wages, fighting for universal childcare and that we fully fund our public schools."

AOC TRIES TO LAUGH OFF 'CRAZY' WOKE ERA AS THING OF THE PAST, BUT CONSERVATIVES AREN'T AMUSED

item.title: Buffalo Bills in damage control mode over their $2.2 billion stadium that is getting crushed online by fans
item.description: The Buffalo Bills are in full crisis management mode after fans posted photos of obstructed views and poor rain coverage at their $2.2 billion stadium.
item.content:encoded:
First, the Buffalo Bills put out a statement on Monday, defending the honor of their new $2.2 billion stadium that was getting absolutely crushed on social media – with photo evidence, no less – for how poorly architects laid out some of the place's sightlines.

Then the club put its chief operating officer and its vice president of stadium development on a conference call with reporters to explain how the fans, some of whom are taxpayers footing $850 million of the cost for the building, didn't have the whole story when they posted those cringe photos of obstructed views and videos of poor rain coverage during the Bills' Saturday practice.

So, yes, the Buffalo Bills are in full crisis management mode right now and the damage control isn't about an injury to a valuable player or a questionable coaching decision.

NY GOVERNOR KATHY HOCHUL TRIES TO GET BILLS CHANT GOING AT NEW STADIUM, COMPLETELY FAILS

It's all about a multibillion-dollar project that, so far, is not quite living up to some of the billing it presented to fans, including personal seat license holders.

"So far, we’ve heard from less than one percent of our PSL holders about anything sightline related," Bills COO Pete Guelli told Western New York area reporters on the conference call Monday. "Relative to that specific issue, we feel very confident what was represented via the virtual venue is accurate to what people saw when they sat in their seats.

"If anybody feels otherwise, we’re taking this on a case-by-case basis, and we’ll address any concerns that they have."

The concerns were all over social media. And they turned what was supposed to be a triumphant moment for a proud franchise into something more closely resembling the season's first loss.

Because, apparently, clear sightlines throughout the facility are beyond the scope of what is possible for a $2.2 billion stadium in 2026.

"Any building you would walk into, there would be some obstructed seating," Guelli explained. "There are seats where we could create a different design, put in a blank area, or they give you the option to put in a seat that might be obstructed for football, but can be used for any other event like a concert. There’s always partial-view or limited-view seats, and we think those were pretty clearly depicted in our virtual venue."

The sight-lines weren't the only problem. Of course not.

Some fans complained their views were blocked by vendors or other fans walking about as the Bills practiced.

JOSH ALLEN DELIVERS FULL-THROATED UNSOLICITED DEFENSE OF BUFFALO BILLS' HIDEOUS NEW UNIFORMS

The club is responding by pointing out that at actual games, fans and vendors will be instructed to wait for the whistle before being allowed to move about. So, yes, the raucous, rowdy Bills crowds that sometimes stood the entire game at the old Highmark Stadium might be going away.

item.title: Shake Shack customer hits 'no tip' at kiosk, then watches prices jump in viral video
item.description: A Shake Shack kiosk appeared to inflate the price of milkshakes after a customer selected the "no tip" option. The viral video reignited tipping debate.
item.content:encoded:
The Utah man behind a viral video appearing to show prices increase at a Shake Shack kiosk after his wife declined to leave a tip says he initially didn't believe her when she told him what had happened.

Brian Powell, 45, told Fox News Digital that he and his wife were waiting to catch a flight out of Salt Lake City when she purchased three milkshakes from the airport's Shake Shack location.

"My wife came to me after buying some shakes and said, 'They charged me more after I didn't tip,'" Powell told Fox News Digital during a Zoom interview from London, where he was vacationing with his wife. "And I thought it was a little interesting."

NO TIPS, WORSE SERVICE? RESTAURANT OWNERS WARN TREND IS 'DEGRADING' DINING EXPERIENCE

Powell said he had visited the location several times before and had never noticed anything similar. Admitting that he was "a bit skeptical," Powell said he returned to the kiosk with his wife and recreated the order while recording the process on his phone.

"We basically went up and duplicated our order, and the same thing happened," Powell said.

The video shows two of the three shakes initially listed at $5.99 each. After "no tip" is selected, the kiosk displays a notice saying there has been a pricing update before the shakes appear at $6.49 each — an increase of 50 cents per drink.

Shake Shack told Fox News Digital the price change was caused by a technology error and that charging customers more for declining to tip is not company policy.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It is not Shake Shack policy, nor that of our licensees, to increase the price of menu items when no tip is added," a spokesperson for the company said.

The airport location is owned and operated by HMSHost, a Shake Shack licensee.

HMSHost investigated and "determined it was an error within their kiosk technology that they have informed us has since been resolved," according to Shake Shack.

"We'll continue working with all our licensed partners to make sure every guest is taken care of at Shake Shack," the spokesperson added.

Powell said that when he recorded the video, he didn't know whether the price change was deliberate or simply a glitch.

"Because I had been to that Shake Shack before, it felt fishy to me, but honestly, I did not know," Powell said. "I mean, the reality is, I've even tipped at that Shake Shack before. … I just thought it was peculiar that, all of a sudden, we were being charged when we pressed 'no tip.'"

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Powell said he never expected the video to attract so much attention. He edited and posted it while waiting for a delayed flight and watched its audience surge after taking off.

"The video has been overwhelming," Powell said, adding that the number of comments flooding his social media inbox made it "impossible" to read through all of them.

Powell's video shines a light on many Americans' larger frustration with tipping prompts at self-service businesses.

"I think my own personal opinion is maybe tipping culture's a little bit out of hand, based on this experience," Powell said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"The entire video was kind of generated by my frustration that, you know, here I was being charged for something I didn't necessarily feel like I should have been charged for."

Powell said he may revisit the kiosk when he returns to Salt Lake City to see if, in fact, the issue has been resolved.

Kelly McGreal of Fox News Digital contributed to this report.

item.title: Why you should back the Indiana Fever to cover the spread against the New York Liberty Tuesday

item.content:encoded:

Best bet: Indiana Fever -2.5 (-106)

item.title: An ultra-rare Cooper Flagg trading card has been found, and the Mavericks are prepared to give a lot for it
item.description: The 1-of-1 Cooper Flagg rookie card from Topps featuring his NBA debut patch was discovered by RhodyBreakers during a live stream card break.
item.content:encoded:
Trading cards have been having a moment ever since COVID — hey, there are worse things to get into when you're locked inside for months — and one of the most sought-after in years has been found.

A 1-of-1 Cooper Flagg rookie card from Topps with the 2025 first pick's NBA Debut patch from his first game has been the holy grail of sports cards as of late, so much so that the Dallas Mavericks put out a "bounty" for it.

Well, according to ESPN, the card has been discovered by RhodyBreakers, some folks that rip open packs of cards on live streams (and if that concept sounds weird to you, it's time to think about scheduling a colonoscopy).

Alright, don't go sticking that one in the spokes of your Huffy so it sounds like a motorcycle.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

There was fervor around a similar card for Pittsburgh Pirates star Paul Skenes, and, as with that one, whoever found it has to decide what to do with the card. The obvious thing is to put it up for auction, because, while the current record for a Cooper Flagg card is $366,000, this one is expected to go for a lot more.

The jersey Flagg wore in his debut — which the patch in the card originally came from — sold for a million dollars at auction, and that's how much some think the card could go for.

But there's also the option of taking the Mavericks "bounty." That comes with two premium season tickets for 32 years, a game-worn jersey (signed), photos with Flagg and the Rookie of the Year trophy, and an all-expenses-paid trip with the team.

WILT CHAMBERLAIN WARM-UP JACKET BOUGHT FOR $3 AT THRIFT STORE SELLS FOR TENS OF THOUSANDS

Tempting... but do you know what can buy a lot of that stuff? A million dollars.

Even though this puppy has been found, it makes me want to go buy a pack of cards. Talk about a hit of pure unleaded dopamine.

Now and then I'll be walking around Target, and I'll pick myself up a pack of IndyCar cards (they exist, and they're awesome) just to feel alive.

You haven't lived until you've pulled an autographed Will Power card out of a $10 box of cards.

Speaking from experience.

item.title: Bron Breakker confronts the future on WWE Raw, Paul Heyman lays down a challenge

item.content:encoded:
The vision for Bron Breakker was clear about a year ago.

He was set to become the new face of WWE to lead the company into the future and eventually hold the World Heavyweight Championship. But injuries, to himself and his stablemates, and the rise of the likes of Oba Femi have appeared to add to the massive chip on his shoulder. And it was presented again during the latest episode of "Monday Night Raw."

Breakker destroyed Joe Hendry in their match last week and took more of his frustrations out on Akira Tozawa, following his loss to Austin Theory. Femi came down to confront Breakker and the two had a faceoff before cooler heads seemed to prevail.

Through all of that, Breakker sought Paul Heyman’s approval and seemed upset that Heyman agreed that Femi was the future of WWE – a designation that Brock Lesnar declared after his Hell in a Cell match against Femi at SummerSlam. Breakker asked Heyman if he thought Femi was the future of WWE.

"Truth be told, I respect Oba Femi. The man did everything he said he was going to do to Brock Lesnar and I have to respect that," Heyman told Breakker without actually answering the question.

Breakker pressed Heyman again.

Heyman gave Breakker something to chew on as he confronts "The Ruler" in the coming weeks.

Breakker has made a tremendous impact since he was called up to the main WWE roster. His devastating torpedo spears have made for viral moments, and he’s captured the intercontinental and tag team titles in his immediate stint on the roster.
